chunks: From him, from Ṣafwān, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Concerning a slave who accuses his wife of fornication while she is a free woman, he said: “They engage in liʿān.” So I said: “Is it on the same footing as the free man?” He said: “Yes.”

key_terms.الْحُرِّ: the free man, used here as the basis of legal comparison
key_terms.امْرَأَتَهُ: his wife, the subject of the accusation
key_terms.حُرَّةٌ: a free woman, indicating her legal status
key_terms.سَوَاءً: equally; with the same legal ruling
key_terms.عَبْدٍ: a male slave; here, the husband making the accusation
key_terms.قَذَفَ: accused of fornication, invoking the legal issue of qadhf
key_terms.يَتَلَاعَنَانِ: the two perform liʿān, the mutual imprecation procedure between spouses

ai.seo_question: Does liʿān apply if a slave accuses his free wife of fornication?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding liʿān when a slave husband accuses his free wife of fornication. Imam Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that the procedure of mutual imprecation applies to them, and that in this matter the slave is treated the same as a free man.
